comments.value: This was an intentional change.  If you feel strongly I suggest you write a feedback post in the Feature Requests category.

details:
Sorry if I'm late in noticing this.  

I don't know if it's an intentional feature or a bug. Can the creators of a world instance kick players from public instances now? 

I was with a couple friends last night and my friend who'd made the public instance noticed he had kick and warn permissions.

Previously, I was under the belief that you only had to worry about getting arbitrarily kicked from a Group Public.

My reason for bring this up is concern about it being abused.

I've been kicked from group publics on several occasions for no apparent reason or for some dumb reason, not for any bad behavior.

For instance, I've joined  a group public and they didn't like my avatar. Kick. Or they don't like that I'm not one of their friends. Kick. Or I'm not a member of the group. Kick.  

Flying in test pilots, I shoot down the group owner without knowing it's the group owner. Kick.

You get the idea.

Anyway, because of this, I am often reluctant to even join a group public instance and would go to regular public instances or to a private instance.

If letting anyone who creates a normal Public instance kick on a whim is intentional, I think this will be likely be abused.

If someone has just created a public, and the number of people in the instance is small, it would discourage people from joining.

Why are you wearing a furry avatar? Kick. Why aren't you wearing a furry avatar? Kick. Why aren't you one of my friends? Kick. I don't like your voice. Kick. 

While not a bad idea in principle, in practice I think it could backfire badly by making people fear being kicked arbitrarily.  It may make public instances with only a few people less attractive for others to join out of fear of being kicked without having done anything wrong.

So, is this intentional or a bug?
title: Instance (Regular Public) Creators Can Kick Now? Bug or Feature?
